column1: # Curated accession -> tip_name alias table (tangle fix, investigations/.../06-auspice-tangle-condition.md).
# Auspice tangles connect tips whose top-level `name` is byte-identical across
# segment trees, so the name must be the segment-independent biological tip ID.
# It is consumed PHYLO-SIDE (phylogenetic/bin/tangle_names.py, after the QC
# gate): ingest ids must stay globally unique in the combined FASTA, so the
# per-segment rename happens where per-segment uniqueness is safe. Key =
# accession.version; a bare accession matches too. Values must be unique
# within each segment's build (tangle_names.py hard-errors on collisions).
# Rows only for multi-record isolates; every value must be a single safe token.
# The S-tip-to-M-tip pairing of the Bardos clones is curator knowledge (Camp
# 2021 S5: HM036208/09/10 = first cloned genome, HM036211/12/13 = second).
# strain code TAHV/58/CZ) - "92" is the isolate number of the 1958 prototype,
# and every spelling below is that one isolate. Bennett Table 1 also
# independently validates the clone pairing above (cl(1)=HM036208-10,
# cl(2)=HM036211-13). The four records here are independent sequencing runs of
# prototype stocks, not the cloned genomes, so they get provenance suffixes
# rather than clone numbers; the two Wadsworth records (U47142.1 S + AF123485.1
# M, same lab/genome project 1996-1999) are paired to give them an S-M tangle
# line; Helsinki (S only) and China CDC (L only) have no cross-segment partner.
